prompt:
Take the first reference photograph and change ONE thing in it: the markings
painted on the road.

Everything else stays exactly as it is: the same Berlin street corner from
the same camera position, the same vertical framing, the same deserted
pavement, the same pedestrian traffic light on its grey pole with the upper
round lens glowing an even plain red, the same pale cream facade with its
stone-framed windows, the same black city bicycles along the wall, the same
granite kerb, the same red bicycle strip with its white bicycle pictogram
running from the kerb toward the bottom of the picture, the same flat
overcast daylight.

THE ONE CHANGE is on the asphalt to the LEFT of the red strip. A pedestrian
crossing of broad white bars is painted there, running in the same direction
as the red strip, from the kerb toward the bottom edge of the picture, the
same bars as in the second reference photograph. The dashed white edge of
the red strip separates the two, so the crossing reads as two lanes side by
side: the white bars on the left for people on foot, the red strip on the
right for bicycles.
